html:
Mixtec Empire is the map's name for the Mixtec kingdoms of Oaxaca in southern Mexico in the centuries before the Spanish conquest. The Mixtecs call their land Ñuu Savi, "land of the rain". It was never one empire but many small kingdoms ruled by related noble families.

These kingdoms are known from their own painted books. Mixtec codices, such as the Codex Zouche-Nuttall, record royal family trees, marriages, wars and rituals. The most famous ruler in them is Eight Deer Jaguar Claw, who united much of the region in the late 1000s and early 1100s before he was killed.

Mixtec artists were the finest goldsmiths of Mesoamerica, and their turquoise mosaic, carved bone and painted pottery were prized across the region. Mixtec nobles moved into the Valley of Oaxaca and married into Zapotec ruling houses. A Mixtec burial placed in Tomb 7 at Monte Albán held one of the richest treasures found in the Americas.

From the mid 1400s the Aztec Triple Alliance conquered many Mixtec kingdoms and took tribute from them. The Spanish arrived in the 1520s. See also Mixtecs and Ñuu Savi.
